To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

decentralized energy production can reduce the costs of the overall electricity supply system if the costs of the decentralized energy production are lower than the costs of the conventional power plants.
• Decentralized supply is not always cost-effective, even if the price of fossil energy carriers is high.

(1) the marginal costs of decentralized energy supply can be significantly higher or lower than the marginal costs of centralized energy supply, and (2) the marginal costs are highly dependent on the characteristics of the decentralized energy supply.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: 1) The impact of decentralized power generation on the overall costs of electricity generation and on the costs of the electricity grid.
the question, whether the integration of decentralized power generation units into the electricity system is beneficial or not, and if so, under which circumstances.
the development of a pricing system that remunerates long-term grid cost saving to operators of decentralized power production or/and charges long-term additional grid cost to these operators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a decentralized supply is only efficient if the decentralized energy generation units are operated in a decentralized manner.
the overall system costs of the electricity system are reduced by decentralized energy generation units and the grid costs are reduced by the decentralized energy units.
decentralized energy supply is beneficial for the overall system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of DG into the existing power generation system is not only possible but that it can even be beneficial for the system if the grid is operated and priced efficiently.
decentralized energy production is a valuable contribution to a sustainable electricity system.
the integration of decentralized supply into the electricity system can be cost-effective if the system is well dimensioned.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the costs or savings from decentralized energy generation depend strongly on the characteristics of the electricity grid and on the characteristics of decentralized supply.

the integration of decentralized supply into the electricity grid is not necessarily a cost driver but can be a cost saver, if the grid is designed appropriately and the decentralized units are remunerated accordingly.
the marginal costs and benefits of decentralization depend strongly on the characteristics of the decentralized supply and the grid.
